record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.context_brief: Positive entropy in smooth convex billiards
record.original_question: Does there exist a strictly convex C1-smooth planar billiard table whose billiard dynamics has positive entropy?

evidence.quote: Задача 2. a) Построить строго выпуклый C1-гладкий биллиардный стол с положительной энтропией.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded planar domain whose boundary $\partial\Omega$ is a simple closed curve of class $C^1$, and assume $\Omega$ is strictly convex (i.e., every chord with endpoints on $\partial\Omega$ lies, except for its endpoints, in the interior of $\Omega$). Consider the billiard dynamics in $\Omega$: a point particle moves in straight lines inside $\Omega$ and reflects elastically off $\partial\Omega$ (angle of incidence equal to angle of reflection). This defines the billiard map $T$ on the phase space $M = \partial\Omega \times (0,\pi)$ of unit tangent vectors pointing inward, equipped with its invariant measure $\sin\varphi\, ds\, d\varphi$.

Question: Does there exist such a strictly convex, $C^1$-smooth billiard table $\Omega$ for which the billiard map $T$ has positive metric (Kolmogorov–Sinai) entropy?
artifact.status_search_result: The construction of a strictly convex $C^1$-smooth planar billiard with positive entropy appears to remain open. Known chaotic smooth-boundary examples (Bunimovich stadium and variants) are only $C^1$ but not strictly convex; smoothing them to $C^2$ regularity creates elliptic periodic orbits, destroying hyperbolicity. Recent results (e.g., by Berger–Turaev and others, 2022–2024) show that generic $C^2$-smooth strictly convex billiards have positive topological entropy, but the strictly convex $C^1$ case with positive metric entropy is not resolved by these constructions.

status_evidence.title: How smooth can convex chaotic billiard tables be?
status_evidence.snippet: Smoothing the stadium boundary to C^2 introduces elliptic periodic orbits, destroying ergodicity; the stadium itself is only C^1 and is not strictly convex.
status_evidence.claim: Existing chaotic smooth-boundary examples are not strictly convex, and smoothing them past C^1 creates elliptic islands.

status_evidence.title: Billiards in generic convex bodies have positive topological entropy
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a C^2 open dense set of convex bodies with smooth boundary whose billiard map has a non-trivial hyperbolic basic set; consequently billiards in generic convex bodies have positive topological entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Positive topological entropy is established for generic strictly convex smooth billiards, but the targeted C^1 metric-entropy question is distinct.

status_evidence.title: Billiard dynamics: An updated survey with the emphasis on open problems
status_evidence.snippet: The problem of constructing a strictly convex C^1-smooth billiard table with positive entropy is listed among open problems in the survey.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as open in a recent billiards survey.
